**The big one.** DERP mode, light that comes from the level's own lamps, skies
with depth, gore, slow motion and a launcher. The [README](https://github.com/robongrui/derp#readme) explains
every feature; this is what changed since v0.77.

**Your graphics settings start fresh.** Too many defaults changed for old
settings to fit, so a `graphics.cfg` from an earlier release is read as
defaults. Keys, mouse and volumes in `doom.cfg` stay as they are.

## The launcher

**DERP.exe** (Windows), **derp** (Linux) and **Play DERP.app** (Mac) now open a
launcher. It finds your game WADs in the `wads` folder, in `DOOMWADDIR` and
`DOOMWADPATH`, and in DOOM and Heretic games installed through Steam or GOG.
Drop WADs, patches, soundtrack packs and SoundFonts on it and each goes where
it belongs. Its Settings page has every F4 option, and **Reset to defaults**
there rescues a setting that keeps the game from starting. It works with a
gamepad.

## DERP mode

F4 → Game → World → Gameplay. Authored is now called DERP and is the default.
It is where the experiments live, and it is unfinished. On id's own maps:

**Monsters that think.** Soldiers work in squads with jobs, take cover behind
corners, kneel behind low walls and fire over them, move one at a time while
the others cover, guard keys, switches and pickups, and pass word of a fight
around. A director paces the pressure. Imps hunt as a pack, jump through
windows they fit (breaking the glass), climb, and hang from the ceiling in dark
corners to drop on your back. Pinkies smell you and charge. Skill levels set
how sharp their aim is and how fast they spot you.

**Monsters that talk.** Soldiers shout what they do, pass on what they know,
chat when they think they are alone and die mid-sentence, each in its own
voice. Imps hiss. The cries ship with the game. The spoken lines are a
separate download, `derp-voices.wad`, attached to this release: put it beside
your game WAD. Without it the soldiers only cry out.

**A player with legs.** You run at Quake's pace, slower than Doomguy. C crouches
and slides out of a run, E jumps, Q kicks, and a kick out of a slide sweeps
the legs. Kicked soldiers get back up with a kip-up.

**Slow motion with a price.** An hourglass beside the status bar holds four
charges. It runs down while the world is slow, and kills fill it back up. The
right mouse button is the shootslide: a slide out of a run into slow motion.

**Heads and guns.** Shots hit the head where the frame draws it, and a pistol
headshot kills quietly. Each gun's bullets have their own speed and spread,
and a round that kills carries on through the body.

## Light

**The whole level is lit as one model.** F4 → Graphics → Lighting → Lighting:
Whole level is the new default. Lamps, screens, windows and the light bouncing
off them light the level, each reaching as far as real light does, and DOOM's
sector light levels no longer light the rooms. It is finished indoors so far.
Classic keeps DOOM's light levels with the bakes on top.

**Monsters block light.** Each monster keeps the light it stands in off the
floor and walls behind it, a separate shadow for every lamp, the sun and every
shot.

**Shot-out lights go dark at once.** The lamps near you are prepared as if
already broken, on helper threads, so the room darkens on the frame the lamp
breaks. Doors left open re-bake their light once they stop.

**Faster bakes.** Light is baked on the graphics card (on a Mac, on the
processor, which is quicker there), and unchanged bake stages come from a
cache on disk, so loads and re-bakes are much quicker.

**More options.** Bumps in all baked light (seams catch the light from the
side it comes from), Flashes light the room, Hero light (off by default; a
small lift for what is nearly black close to you), Eye adaptation metered off
the picture, and Fill light and Surfaces return light for the whole-level
model.

**HDR.** F4 → Graphics → Display → HDR. On an HDR display, lamps, fire,
muzzle flashes and glowing pickups rise past white while walls and the HUD stay
as in SDR. HDR in the scene lets lit walls and highlights rise too, and HDR
colours can be vivid as on the Steam Deck OLED.

## Skies and weather

**Sky depth.** Painted mountains stand at their own distances and shift as you
move, with valley mist between them. DOOM's rocky skies become karst towers,
DOOM II's city becomes buildings, hell's skies get wind-blown flames, and cloud
skies get volumetric clouds that follow the weather, the hour and the wind.
Heretic's episodes 4 and 5 get skies of their own. **Sky: Cached** paints the
sky a little at a time and costs far less.

**Sunshower.** Light rain with the sun out breaks the cloud and puts a rainbow
opposite the sun.

**More weather.** Firestorm (sparks and soot over a burning city), Random (each
map rolls its own climate), an Amount choice from a light shower to a
downpour, and Lamps light the weather, which gives snow, sand and ash a lamp's
colour around it.

## Combat

**Gore.** F4 → Game → World → Gore, on by default. Killing blows tear bodies
apart, wounds go to the bone, big monsters can be cut in two and a rocket into
a cacodemon's mouth pops it. With Tear fibres a torn-off part hangs on by
fibres that stretch and snap, made for slow motion. It changes the game's
rules, so it is off in demos and netgames.

**Slow motion.** F4 → Graphics → Combat → Slow motion: on a key (X or F12) or
when shooting. The world runs at a quarter of its speed, bullets visibly fly,
and you keep aiming at full speed.

**Muzzle flash.** Bullet guns throw a burst of fire and smoke off the barrel,
never the same shape twice, yours and the zombies'.

**Explosions.** Four styles: DOOM's sprite, Doom-like (the default: a bigger
fireball with sparks, smoke, a scorch and a light that lingers), Physical (the
blast's gas simulated in the room, which shapes it) and Flashbulb (a tic of
white light and fast sparks).

**Bullet impacts.** Shots throw what the wall is made of: concrete dust,
wood splinters, metal sparks.

**Deaths and blood.** Ragdoll pixels picks how a ragdoll is turned back into
DOOM pixels, trading crispness for less flicker. Ragdolls go over low walls,
down stairs and skid on ice, and soldiers killed kneeling fall from the kneel.
Blood pools run down steps, and blood behaves like itself in water, nukage,
lava, snow and sand.

## Sound

**Room tails traced from the map.** In DERP mode each room's ringing can be
traced from its real walls and materials, far rooms ring through their
doorways, and the room can be measured once at level start.

**Recorded soundtracks.** F4 → Sound → Music → Soundtrack plays the PlayStation
(`HQPSXMUS.WAD`), 3DO, or the 2024 re-release's IDKFA remix and recorded
originals (`extras.wad`) from packs you own.

**New sound defaults.** Room acoustics, ambience, traced room tails and far
rooms are now off by default. Together they were most of the mixer's work. Turn
them on under F4 → Sound for the full soundscape.

## Looks and screen

- **Presets and cost bars.** F4 → Graphics → Display → Preset sets every
  costly option at once: Lowest, Handheld (for the Steam Deck), Balanced, High
  or Everything. Bars beside options show what they cost.
- **Status bar size and width.** Smaller sizes stay pixel-exact; full width
  uses the wide bar's sides from the 2019 and later IWADs.
- **Pickup flash by item.** Health flashes green, armour blue, keys in their
  own colour. Pickups also catch a passing glint.
- **Show FPS: Full, with GPU times** shows what each part of the picture
  costs.
- With partial invisibility your hands turn to a spectre's fuzz, and the
  automap marks what the 3D view has seen.

## Faster and fixed

- One BSP walk per frame, smaller shaders for Apple GPUs, and lifts no longer
  cost frames in rooms with glowing walls.
- The Steam Deck's lamp bake no longer goes wrong.
- Classic aim now says what it does: with it off, rockets, plasma and BFG balls
  fly along the view like bullets.

## Known issues

- **Odd lighting after a mid-level change.** A light switch or similar change
  in the middle of a level can light the area oddly.
- **Black panels.** Some textures can turn black.

Both can happen at any time, and both fix themselves when you cycle through
the presets in F4 → Graphics → Display → Preset. The cause is still being
looked for.

## Credits

DERP mode's voices and cries were generated with ElevenLabs and edited for the
game; they have their own licence (`licenses/VOICES.txt`). The kick's leg and
the kneeling soldiers are stand-in art generated with ChatGPT, the soldiers
drawn after id Software's zombieman and shotgun guy.
